maya: Heads-up — onboarding magellan-70k (int4v2) into long-context fuzzbench. After ~28k tokens we see a repeating token-shift pattern and KV cache divergence. Also a small latency bump (~30ms).
ben: Which quant/profile + RoPE scaling? Is this reproducible on CPU eval? :thinking:
maya: int4v2, default rope_scale=dynamic, reproducer is stable on GPU local. Not seen on short sequences. I ran with batch=1 and streaming off.
alina: can you paste the minimal repro command? I'll try on my machine.
maya: repro:
```
./run_fuzz.sh --model magellan-70k --quant int4v2 --seq 70000 --batch 1 --seed 42 --mode fuzzbench
```
Log excerpt around the divergence:
```
[kvcache] pos=28652 expected_index=28652 got_index=28653
[kvcache] stitch_mismatch shard=3 span=128 discrepancy=1
[token] emitted: "the" -> later emitted: "\n"
latency: 168ms -> 198ms at pos ~28660
```
ben: That index bump + emitted token swap smells like a RoPE wrap/offset misapply during KV writeback. Maybe a boundary condition when phase wraps beyond 2*pi for large pos.
sasha: Also can be triggered by eviction heuristics — if prefix evicted asynchronously, reads might shift indexes. What eviction policy on your run? maya: default LRU with async background compaction.
dave: Try forcing synchronous eviction or disabling compaction. If divergence disappears, it's a race between prefill and compaction.
maya: quick test: set KV_COMPACTION=0 KV_EVICT_SYNC=1 -> divergence still happens but later (~pos 32900). So compaction not sole cause.
alina: I suspect RoPE scaling interpolation with quantized kernels. On int4 paths we use approximated sin/cos LUT and smaller accumulator; maybe rounding accumulates at high pos. Try ROPE_SCALE=1 (no dynamic scaling) and ROPE_MODE=wrap-check.
maya: ran with ROPE_SCALE=linear and ROPE_MODE=wrap-check — pattern changed: shift occurs earlier but signature of errors different (mismatched token context rather than simple index bump).
triage-bot: Incident created: IN-177999-ROPE-FUZZ. Linked to run 1779991234.
ops-bot: Snapshot saved at s3://redwood-ci/magellan-onboard/1779991234/snap.tar.gz (tags: int4v2,fuzzbench)
alina: action plan proposal:
- alina to bisect between quant kernels (int4v2 scalar vs vector) by running small window reproducer
- ben to add assertions in kvcache writer/reader to log shard+pos checksums
- sasha to try disabling KV prefetch and running with full sync eviction
- maya to run a golden-run on fp16 to confirm it's quant-only
maya: I'll run fp16 now and post results.
maya: fp16 run finished — no divergence up to 70k tokens. So this is quant-path specific.
alina: ok that narrows it. Ben, can you instrument the quant fused-kernel to emit a checksum of rotary alignment every 1k tokens? Something cheap.
ben: yes, will push a patch to the magellan branch:```
diff --git a/infer/kernels/rotary_quant.cu b/infer/kernels/rotary_quant.cu
+ // emit alignment checksum to stdout when DEBUG_ROPE_CHECK=1
```
ben: patch pushed, running now.
dave: small note — add a nondestructive fast checksum so we don't slow throughput too much.
maya: latest run with the checksum shows a diverging checksum at pos 28653 which correlates with the index mismatch. Looks like quant rounding in sin/cos followed by cast to int16 for index calc.
sasha: if rounding/accumulation is the root, maybe we can try higher-precision intermediate or periodic re-normalization of phase before writing KV.
alina: agree. I'll prototype an interim fix to renormalize phase every 4k tokens and see if it mitigates.
maya: summary of immediate findings:
- Divergence reproducible on int4v2 path only
- fp16 path clean up to 70k
- Index bump + checksum change at ~28.6k correlates with emitted token mismatch
- Compaction/eviction not sole cause but may influence timing
- Next: bisect kernel impl, add logging and try periodic phase renorm
alina: assigning owners in thread: alina (bisect + renorm prototype), ben (kernel checksum instrumentation), sasha (eviction/prefetch experiments), maya (full fuzz runs + golden fp16)
maya: thanks all — will report back with bisect results. :thumbsup:"
